processing.input_quantity: gamma0 backscatter, linear power, radiometrically terrain corrected (ASF GCOV docs)
processing.registration_note: Registration is identical for both dates (same grid), so dB differences are unaffected; only absolute map placement may be off by up to half a native pixel.

statistics.method: Paired L-band gamma0 differences in dB on a common grid after incoherent multilooking; per-channel gate T = max(floor_db, sigma * 1.4826 * MAD); no median-shift correction.

as_reported.description: gates centred on 0 dB (no shift correction)

median_centred.description: differences re-centred on the scene median before gating (assumes the median shift is NOT a real change)

floor_only_3db.description: fixed 3 dB gates, no shift correction

diagnostics.interpretation_note: A positive median shift that appears in every tile and stratum cannot be separated, with two dates and no stable reference targets, into real widespread change (wetter soils, vegetation water content, inundation), acquisition conditions, or a residual radiometric offset between PROVISIONAL products.

hypotheses.label: HH increase exceeding HV increase
hypotheses.consistent_with: New or deeper water beneath emergent vegetation (enhanced double-bounce).
alternatives: Wet or flattened vegetation changing stem orientation
Speckle or residual geolocation error at boundaries

hypotheses.label: HH and HV both decrease
hypotheses.consistent_with: Transition toward smooth open water (specular reflection) or vegetation submergence.
alternatives: Vegetation loss by burning, grazing or cutting
Drying of a previously wet rough surface
Calm-wind conditions on existing water (wind roughening on the earlier date)

hypotheses.label: Other large change
hypotheses.rule: |dHH| >= T_HH or |dHV| >= T_HV, not in the classes above

overlays.note: Display-only reprojection to EPSG:4326; statistics computed on native UTM grid.

nasa_power.source: NASA POWER Daily API v2.10.3 (source native resolution)
limits: Point value from coarse reanalysis/satellite-derived grids (order of 0.5 deg); not a rain-gauge measurement and not local to every AOI pixel.
Rainfall over the AOI is only one driver of Sudd inundation; upstream White Nile inflow (Lake Victoria/Albert outflow) dominates the swamp water balance.
Cloud amount is context for optical-imagery limitations; it does not prove that any specific optical image was unusable.
CLOUD_AMT returned fill values (-999) after 2026-08-30 at retrieval time.

warnings: Scene-wide median change is large (dHH=+1.08 dB, dHV=+0.50 dB). This may reflect a real widespread change (e.g. seasonal inundation or vegetation growth) OR a radiometric/geometry/moisture effect; no correction was applied.
maturity_note: PROVISIONAL (CRID P05023): calibrated, validation at limited sites; to be superseded by 2027 reprocessing.
limitations: Candidate radar backscatter change only: no class is a confirmed flood, wetland conversion or damage.
No independent inundation reference (gauge, field survey or validated water map) was compared in this run.
Thresholds are heuristic screening gates, not calibrated probabilities or accuracies.
PROVISIONAL products (CRID P05023) may change in the announced 2027 reprocessing.
Speckle is reduced by multilooking but not eliminated; isolated cells may be noise.
Equatorial ionospheric effects, wind on open water and rain on canopy can alter L-band backscatter.
Only two dates are compared in the primary analysis; the scene-wide positive shift cannot be attributed to a single cause.
